newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end lower, pausing after records.
newsitem.headline: German shares end lower, pausing after records.

text.p: German shares ended dealings lower on Wednesday, taking a breather after their record-breaking rally the day before and discouraged by weakness on foreign markets.

The DAX index of 30 leading shares closed floor trade down 13.61 points, or 0.48 percent, at 2,797.03, not managing to hold above the crucial 2,800 point level, which it had managed to penetrate decisively for the first time on Tuesday.
German Bund strength had been supportive for the market in early dealings as the December Bund future made an all-time high of 101.55.
But the contract later pared gains after U.S. durable goods data came in stronger than expected, reviving some inflation worries and putting pressure on bond and share markets.

The IBIS DAX index, measuring all-day electronic trade in the DAX index, ended down 14.76 points, or 0.53 percent, at 2,793.86 points as Wall Street started weaker and German bonds lost most of their sheen.
But dealers said that the upward trend in the DAX was still intact and that a slight correction was perfectly healthy for the market.

Dealers said the day's main focus had been shares in Europe's largest carmaker Volkswagen AG, which slipped almost six percent, or 37.70 marks to 601.25 marks in bourse trade, after a U.S. judge denied VW's motion to dismiss racketeering claims by rival Opel.
The ruling could open VW to potentially higher damages in the lawsuit with Opel, a subsidiary of U.S. carmaker General Motors.
VW shares were also under pressure after the firm said it could introduce short-time working hours at its main plant because a French truck blockade has hit the supply of car parts.

Dealers said VW's losses had weighed on the whole market and on other shares in the car sector in particular. BMW AG ended bourse dealings down nine marks at 976 marks and Daimler-Benz AG was 1.23 marks off at 98.65 marks.
Dealers said trade volume was likely to be thinner than normal on Thursday with markets closed in the U.S. for the Thanksgiving holiday.
